subject.title: [Feature]: [Feature Request] 按用户维度统计 Token 使用量

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class per-user token usage accounting in core, and what canonical principal should usage attribution use?
rationale: The request crosses identity, privacy, storage, Gateway RPC, Dashboard, `/usage`, and quota/billing policy, while current Gateway docs describe a trusted-operator boundary rather than tenant-style users.

options.title: Design core identity accounting
options.body: Define the principal model, authorization, retention/redaction rules, storage schema, Gateway RPC shape, and UI exposure before implementation.

options.title: Keep reporting in front-layer or plugin integrations first
options.body: Leave core usage grouped by existing dimensions while Pinchy-style front layers or plugins map their own authenticated users to usage records.

options.title: Decline multi-user accounting for now
options.body: Keep OpenClaw scoped to the current single-operator usage model and close related multi-user accounting requests as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design core identity accounting
recommendation.body: Define the principal model, authorization, retention/redaction rules, storage schema, Gateway RPC shape, and UI exposure before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The usage/cost accounting history and broad core surface make this the strongest routing signal among the identified owners.
